killer.name: INVERTIBLE_XOR_REENCODING_CYCLE
killer.conclusion: reversible definitional re-encoding changes representation but removes zero unresolved semantic information

anti_alias_theorem: Any progress potential invariant under exact bijective definitional re-encoding is constant on a reversible re-encoding cycle; therefore it cannot strictly decrease at every macro-step if those re-encodings are admitted as macro-steps.

semantic_reference.N_R: number of distinct residual continuation relations after fixing the live interface
semantic_reference.invariance: bijective live-interface reparameterization preserves N_R and mu
semantic_reference.authority: checker/reference only; no polynomial-time computability claim

successor_rule: reversible normalization/re-encoding steps live inside one quotient class and may claim zero progress; strict decrease is reserved for certified irreversible quotient transitions
